title: Triclosan induces cardiac malformations via an estrogen receptor-ERK-mitochondrial apoptotic signaling axis in zebrafish embryos.
authors: Fu, Jing; Chen, Jin; He, Yaolin; Li, Wenzhuo; Ren, Jing; Shen, Yongkang; Tang, Ningman; Liu, Anfei; Gao, Yi; Huang, Ming; Liu, Zhenzhong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究三氯生通过雌激素受体-ERK-线粒体凋亡通路诱导斑马鱼心脏畸形，属于环境毒理学与发育生物学，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Triclosan (TCS), a widely used antimicrobial agent, is persistently detected in aquatic environments (up to 1.14 muM in pore water) and human matrices, raising concerns about its developmental toxicity. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying TCS-induced cardiac malformations remain largely unresolved. Here, we report that exposure of zebrafish embryos to TCS at concentrations including environmentally relevant levels (62.5 nM to 1 muM) induced cardiac morphological abnormalities and cardiomyocyte apoptosis, accompanied by transcriptomic alterations in genes associated with cardiac development and apoptosis. Mechanistic investigations revealed that TCS activated ERalpha and the membrane estrogen receptor GPER, resulting in sustained ERK1/2 phosphorylation. Pharmacological blockade of ER or ERK signaling, as well as genetic knockdown of esr1/esr2a, effectively rescued TCS-induced cardiac malformations and apoptotic responses, supporting the involvement of ER-ERK signaling in TCS-associated cardiac abnormalities. Notably, ER-ERK activation triggered profound mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by excessive mitochondrial ROS generation, dissipation of mitochondrial membrane potential, and ultrastructural mitochondrial damage, ultimately leading to cleaved-caspase-3-dependent apoptosis. The mitochondrial-targeted antioxidant MitoQ significantly alleviated ROS generation, mitochondrial injury, and cardiac defects. Furthermore, molecular docking analysis supported strong binding affinities between TCS and key components of the ER-ERK signaling axis, suggesting potential molecular interactions. Overall, this study identifies a previously unrecognized ER-ERK-mitochondrial apoptotic pathway as a central mechanism driving TCS-induced cardiac developmental toxicity, providing mechanistic insight into the cardiovascular developmental risks posed by environmental endocrine disruptors.
abstract_zh: 三氯生（TCS）作为一种广泛使用的抗菌剂，在水生环境（孔隙水中浓度高达1.14 μM）及人体基质中持续被检出，引发对其发育毒性的关注。然而，TCS诱导心脏畸形的分子机制在很大程度上仍未阐明。在此，我们报告，将斑马鱼胚胎暴露于包括环境相关浓度（62.5 nM至1 μM）在内的TCS浓度下，可诱导心脏形态异常和心肌细胞凋亡，并伴随与心脏发育和凋亡相关基因的转录组改变。机制研究表明，TCS激活了ERα和膜雌激素受体GPER，导致ERK1/2持续磷酸化。药理学阻断ER或ERK信号通路，以及基因敲低esr1/esr2a，均能有效挽救TCS诱导的心脏畸形和凋亡反应，支持ER-ERK信号参与TCS相关心脏异常。值得注意的是，ER-ERK激活引发了显著的线粒体功能障碍，其特征为过量线粒体ROS生成、线粒体膜电位消散及线粒体超微结构损伤，最终导致cleaved-caspase-3依赖性凋亡。线粒体靶向抗氧化剂MitoQ显著减轻了ROS生成、线粒体损伤及心脏缺陷。此外，分子对接分析支持TCS与ER-ERK信号轴关键组分之间的强结合亲和力，提示潜在的分子相互作用。总体而言，本研究识别出一条先前未被认识的ER-ERK-线粒体凋亡通路，作为驱动TCS诱导心脏发育毒性的核心机制，为环境内分泌干扰物对心血管发育风险提供了机制性见解。
